parsed.why: No criminalisation and trans discrimination protection nominally remain, but state-imposed exposure is documented: birth-sex strip-search policy, prison placement by birth sex, ward exclusion (a documented death in a side room), and a statutory single-sex-spaces code covering hostels and changing rooms. Hostile courts, no working remedy.

Documented presentation-based arrests and cross-dressing convictions, police sexual coercion with impunity, criminalised advocacy reaching gender expression, no marker change or anti-discrimination law, abusive custody and care denial. Police described as merciless toward LGBT tourists; consequences near-catastrophic if outed.

No criminalisation and a constitutional equality guarantee (sexual orientation only); thin record with dated societal stigma and no documented trans-specific targeting. But no documented recourse, no protection for gender identity, conservative local climate, and silence here is not safety.

No criminalisation, courts have granted trans-specific relief, community infrastructure and pride exist. Offset by documented public-space discrimination and physical/sexual harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities, rising political hostility and death threats, and slow litigation-only recourse.

Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 10 years) and recently upheld; no anti-discrimination law, no recognition, no LGBT organisation or support. Cross-dressing people assaulted and a trans teen charged with fraud. Police enforcement frequency undocumented, limiting further deduction.
